name: pve_mcp_info
title: About this server
description: Says what this server allows, per cluster: read-only or not, elevated changes, guest execution, SSH, sensitive data, dry run, protected guests, which toolsets are loaded and how many tools. Call this first.

name: pve_overview
title: Cluster overview
description: The state of the cluster in one answer: version, quorum, nodes, guest counts, storage usage, HA and recent failed tasks. Whatever could not be read is named in "unavailable". A token only sees what it has audit rights on, so counts may be partial.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_find_guest
title: Find a guest
description: Finds VMs and containers by vmid, name, tag, status, node, type or IP address, across the cluster. An IP can only be read from a running LXC or from a running VM with its guest agent: those that could not be checked are listed in ip_not_checked, so no match does not mean the address is free.

name.description: Part of the name, in any case.

tag.description: A whole tag, in any case.

node.description: Only guests on this node.

type.description: qemu for VMs, lxc for containers.

ip.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, without prefix length.

include_ips.description: Also read the addresses of each running guest found. One request per guest. Implied by ip.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_wait_task
title: Wait for a task
description: Waits for a task (UPID) to end and gives its result with the end of its log. A failed task is an error, task_failed. A task that outlasts the wait comes back with still_running: it goes on and is not cancelled.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

name: pve_get_task_log_tail
title: End of a task log
description: The status of a task and the last lines of its log, without having to page through it. The log is untrusted text.

lines.description: How many lines, from the end. Default 50.

name: pve_guest_power
title: Start or stop a guest
description: Starts, shuts down, stops or reboots a VM or a container from its vmid, finds the node and the type, and waits for the task. stop cuts the power at once, as pulling the plug would; shutdown asks the guest to stop cleanly. Destructive except for start. A guest that is already in the requested state is left alone.

action.description: What to do.

timeout.description: For shutdown and reboot: seconds the guest has to comply.

force_stop.description: For shutdown: stop the guest hard when it did not comply within the timeout.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_snapshot_guest
title: Snapshot a guest
description: Takes a snapshot of a VM or a container from its vmid and waits for the task. Only VMs can include their memory.

description.description: A note kept with the snapshot.

vmstate.description: VMs only: save the memory too.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_list_guest_snapshots
title: List the snapshots of a guest
description: The snapshots of a VM or a container from its vmid, oldest first, and which one the guest currently runs from. The "current" entry of the API is not a snapshot and is left out of rows.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

annotations.title: List the snapshots of a guest

name: pve_provision_lxc
title: Provision a container
description: Creates a container from start to finish: free vmid, template found on a storage or downloaded from the appliance index, creation, start, IP address. Each step is reported. If one fails, the error says what was created and what remains: nothing is ever deleted automatically. It never replaces an existing guest. The password is never returned.

template.description: A volume such as local:vztmpl/debian-12-standard_12.7-1_amd64.tar.zst, or a name or start of name such as debian-12-standard, looked up on the storages of the node and then in the appliance index.

node.description: The node. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

vmid.description: The id to use. Default: the next free one.

disk_gb.description: Size of the root disk in GiB. Needs storage.

template_storage.description: Storage to look for the template on and to download it to. Default: the storages of the node that accept templates.

download_template.description: Download the template when it is not on the node. Default true.

net0.description: First network interface, as a Proxmox property string. Default: name=eth0,bridge=vmbr0,ip=dhcp.

ssh_public_keys.description: Public SSH keys for root, one per line.

password.description: Root password of the container. Never returned nor logged.

unprivileged.description: Run as an unprivileged container. Default true, which is safer than the Proxmox default.

features.description: Features as a property string, such as nesting=1.

description.description: Notes.

start.description: Start it at the end. Default true.

ip_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for an IP address after the start. Default 30.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for each task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this the job stops and reports what remains.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

name: pve_provision_vm_from_template
title: Provision a VM from a template
description: Makes a VM from a VM template from start to finish: clone, cloud-init (ciuser, cipassword, sshkeys, ipconfig0), disk resize, start, wait for the guest agent. Each step is reported. If one fails, the error says what was created and what remains: nothing is ever deleted automatically. It never replaces an existing guest. The password is never returned.

template_vmid.description: The vmid of the VM template to clone.

newid.description: The id of the new VM. Default: the next free one.

target_node.description: Node of the new VM. Default: the template's. A different node needs storage the target can reach.

full.description: Full copy rather than linked clone. Implied by storage.

description.description: Notes.

cipassword.description: Cloud-init password. Never returned nor logged.

sshkeys.description: Public SSH keys for cloud-init, one per line, in plain text.

ipconfig0.description: Cloud-init address of the first interface, such as ip=dhcp or ip=10.0.0.5/24,gw=10.0.0.1.

enable_agent.description: Set agent=1 on the new VM. The guest system still has to run qemu-guest-agent.

disk.description: Disk to resize. Default: the first disk of the boot order.

disk_size.description: New size such as 40G, or growth such as +10G. Disks cannot shrink.

start.description: Start it at the end. Default true.

agent_wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the guest agent after the start. Default 120. 0 does not wait.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for each task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this the job stops and reports what remains.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

annotations.title: Provision a VM from a template

name: pve_health_check
title: Health check
description: Checks nodes, quorum, storage usage, failed services, failed tasks, HA, Ceph if there is any, replication and subscriptions. Each finding has a severity, the object, the evidence and a suggested action. Sections that could not be read are in "unavailable" and are not counted as healthy: overall says "incomplete" rather than good news. The thresholds used are returned with the answer.

storage_warn_percent.description: Usage from which a storage or root disk is a warning. Default 85.

storage_critical_percent.description: Usage from which it is critical. Default 95.

memory_warn_percent.description: Node memory usage from which it is a warning. Default 90.

task_hours.description: How far back failed tasks count, in hours. Default 24.

name: pve_security_audit
title: Security audit
description: Reads the security-related settings: firewall state (cluster, nodes, guests), privileged containers, API tokens without expiry or privilege separation, second factor on root@pam, powerful ACLs on /, backups, pending updates, certificate expiry. Findings state what the data shows, with evidence and a suggested action. Sections it could not read are named in "unavailable". This is neither a certification nor a statement of compliance, and only sees what this token may read.

cert_warn_days.description: Days before expiry from which a certificate is a finding. Default 30.

include_guests.description: Also read the config and firewall options of each guest. Two requests per guest. Default true.

name: pve_backup_coverage
title: Backup coverage
description: For each guest: whether it is in a backup job, and the age of its last backup found on the backup storages. Also the jobs and the guests that no job covers. A storage or node that could not be read is named in "unavailable", and a guest whose last backup could therefore be missed is listed under not_determined instead of being called unprotected. Having a backup says nothing of whether it restores.

max_age_days.description: A last backup older than this is a finding. Default 7.

page_limit.description: Rows per page. Default: as many as fit in the answer.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_capacity_report
title: Capacity report
description: CPU, memory and disk per node, what the guests are allocated against that (overcommit ratios), storage usage with a straight-line forecast from its history, and the biggest guests. Facts and ratios only: no threshold judges them. Sections that could not be read are in "unavailable".

forecast_window.description: History the storage forecast is based on. Default month.

forecast.description: Read the history of each storage for a forecast. One request per storage. Default true.

top.description: How many guests in each list of the biggest. Default 5.

[POST /access/domains/{realm}/sync. Needs: (Realm.AllocateUser on /access/realm/{realm} and User.Modify on /access/groups). full.description: DEPRECATED: use 'remove-vanished' instead. If set, uses the LDAP Directory as source of truth, deleting users or groups not returned from the sync and removing all locally modified properties of synced users. If not set, only syncs information which is present in the synced data, and does not delete or modify anything else.

purge.description: DEPRECATED: use 'remove-vanished' instead. Remove ACLs for users or groups which were removed from the config during a sync.

name: pve_bulk_restart_cluster_ceph_services
title: Bulk restart cluster ceph services
description: Cluster-wide rolling restart of all Ceph daemons of the given type. For MON/MGR/MDS each daemon is restarted only after Ceph reports the previous one is back up and the next one is safe to stop. For OSDs the cluster path orchestrates the per-node endpoint at /nodes/{node}/ceph/restart-bulk on each node in turn, inheriting that endpoint's per-OSD 'noout' handling and resume support. ... [POST /cluster/ceph/restart-bulk. Needs: Sys.Modify on /. Destructive.]

dry-run.description: Log the plan (which daemons would be restarted, in what order) without actually doing anything. Default: 0.

force.description: Proceed past a HEALTH_WARN with non-benign checks like PG_DEGRADED, SLOW_OPS, or MON_DOWN. A blocking HEALTH_ERR is fatal regardless of this flag. Checks that ceph reports as muted, and checks known to be harmless for a rolling restart, never block and are named in the task log. ... Default: 0.

only-outdated.description: OSDs only: restart only OSDs whose running version differs from the locally-installed ceph-osd binary on their host. Forwarded to each per-node sub-task so the per-host installed version is used (a partial upgrade where one host is on a newer build is handled correctly). Default: 0.

service-type.description: Ceph daemon type to restart cluster-wide.

timeout.description: Per-daemon timeout (in seconds) for the up-wait phase. Note: for daemons on remote nodes the same timeout also bounds the remote restart task, so the per-daemon budget can be up to 2x this value. Default sized for slow MDS journal replay or MON paxos settle on busy clusters; bump higher if the cluster routinely takes longer to stabilize after a daemon restart. Default: 600. bwlimit.description: Set I/O bandwidth limit for various operations (in KiB/s). Property string (key=value,...; * required): clone=<LIMIT> default=<LIMIT> migration=<LIMIT> move=<LIMIT> restore=<LIMIT>

consent-text.description: Consent text that is displayed before logging in.

console.description: Select the default Console viewer. You can either use the builtin java applet (VNC; deprecated and maps to html5), an external virt-viewer comtatible application (SPICE), an HTML5 based vnc viewer (noVNC), or an HTML5 based console client (xtermjs). If the selected viewer is not available (e.g. SPICE not activated for the VM), the fallback is noVNC.

crs.description: Cluster resource scheduling settings. Property string (key=value,...; * required): ha=<basic|static|dynamic> ha-auto-rebalance=<boolean> ha-auto-rebalance-hold-duration=<number> ha-auto-rebalance-margin=<number> ha-auto-rebalance-method=<bruteforce|topsis> ha-auto-rebalance-threshold=<number> ha-rebalance-on-start=<boolean>

delete.description: A list of settings you want to delete.

description.description: Datacenter description. Shown in the web-interface datacenter notes panel. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

email_from.description: Specify email address to send notification from (default is root@$hostname)

fencing.description: Set the fencing mode of the HA cluster. Hardware mode needs a valid configuration of fence devices in /etc/pve/ha/fence.cfg. With both all two modes are used. WARNING: 'hardware' and 'both' are EXPERIMENTAL & WIP Default: watchdog.

ha.description: Cluster wide HA settings. Property string (key=value,...; * required): shutdown_policy*=<freeze|failover|conditional|migrate>

http_proxy.description: Specify external http proxy which is used for downloads (example: 'http://username:password@host:port/') Pattern: http://.*

keyboard.description: Default keybord layout for vnc server.

location.description: The location of the cluster. Format: latitude=<number> ,longitude=<number> [,name=<name>].

mac_prefix.description: Prefix for the auto-generated MAC addresses of virtual guests. The default 'BC:24:11' is the OUI assigned by the IEEE to Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH for a 24-bit large MAC block. You're allowed to use this in local networks, i.e., those not directly reachable by the public (e.g., in a LAN or behind NAT). Default: BC:24:11.

max_workers.description: Defines how many workers (per node) are maximal started on actions like 'stopall VMs' or task from the ha-manager. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

migration.description: For cluster wide migration settings. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type*=<secure|insecure> network=<CIDR>

migration_unsecure.description: Migration is secure using SSH tunnel by default. For secure private networks you can disable it to speed up migration. Deprecated, use the 'migration' property instead!

next-id.description: Control the range for the free VMID auto-selection pool. Property string (key=value,...; * required): lower=<integer> upper=<integer>

notify.description: Cluster-wide notification settings. Property string (key=value,...; * required): fencing=<always|never> package-updates=<auto|always|never> replication=<always|never> target-fencing=<TARGET> target-package-updates=<TARGET> target-replication=<TARGET>

registered-tags.description: A list of tags that require a `Sys.Modify` on '/' to set and delete. Tags set here that are also in 'user-tag-access' also require `Sys.Modify`. Format: <tag>[;<tag>...]. Pattern: (?:(?^i:[a-z0-9_][a-z0-9_\-\+\.]*);)*(?^i:[a-z0-9_][a-z0-9_\-\+\.]*)

replication.description: For cluster wide replication settings. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type*=<secure|insecure> network=<CIDR>

tag-style.description: Tag style options. Property string (key=value,...; * required): case-sensitive=<boolean> color-map=<string> ordering=<config|alphabetical> shape=<full|circle|dense|none>

u2f.description: u2f Property string (key=value,...; * required): appid=<APPID> origin=<URL>

user-tag-access.description: Privilege options for user-settable tags Property string (key=value,...; * required): user-allow=<none|list|existing|free> user-allow-list=<string>

webauthn.description: webauthn configuration Property string (key=value,...; * required): allow-subdomains=<boolean> id=<DOMAINNAME> origin=<URL> rp=<RELYING_PARTY>

cputype.description: Name for the custom CPU model. The 'custom-' prefix is optional.

flags.description: List of additional CPU flags separated by ';'. Use '+FLAG' to enable, '-FLAG' to disable a flag. There is a special 'nested-virt' shorthand which controls nested virtualization for the current CPU ('svm' for AMD and 'vmx' for Intel). Custom CPU models can specify any flag supported by QEMU/KVM, VM-specific flags must be from the following set for security reasons: aes, amd-no-ssb, amd-ssbd, ... Pattern: (?^u:(?^u:([+-])([a-zA-Z0-9\-_\.]+))(;(?^u:([+-])([a-zA-Z0-9\-_\.]+)))*)

guest-phys-bits.description: Number of physical address bits available to the guest. Format: <integer> (32 - 64).

hidden.description: Do not identify as a KVM virtual machine. Only affects vCPUs with x86-64 architecture. Default: 0.

hv-vendor-id.description: The Hyper-V vendor ID. Some drivers or programs inside Windows guests need a specific ID. Pattern: (?^u:[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,12})

level.description: Maximum input value for the basic CPUID leaves the guest can query - that is the vendor (leaf 0), family/model/stepping and feature bits (leaf 1), cache and topology info (leaves 4 and B), and so on. Higher-numbered leaves are hidden. Setting '30' is a common workaround for Hyper-V boot failures on Windows guests running on recent Intel hosts. Only applies when the vCPU architecture is x86_64. Format: <integer> (0 - 4294967295).

phys-bits.description: The physical memory address bits that are reported to the guest OS. Should be smaller or equal to the host's. Set to 'host' to use value from host CPU, but note that doing so will break live migration to CPUs with other values. Format: <8-64|host>.

reported-model.description: CPU model and vendor to report to the guest. Must be a QEMU/KVM supported model. Only valid for custom CPU model definitions, default models will always report themselves to the guest OS. Default: kvm64.

name: pve_bulk_restart_node_ceph_services
title: Bulk restart node ceph services
description: Rolling restart of all Ceph OSDs on this node. Each OSD is restarted only after Ceph reports the previous one is back up and the next one is safe to stop. For non-OSD Ceph daemons, use the cluster-wide endpoint at /cluster/ceph/restart-bulk. The 'noout' flag is applied only to the OSDs targeted by this run, so unrelated OSDs on other nodes that fail during the restart window still get out-marked normally. ... [POST /nodes/{node}/ceph/restart-bulk. Needs: Sys.Modify on /. Destructive.]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

dry-run.description: Log the plan (which OSDs would be restarted, in what order) without actually doing anything. Default: 0.

force.description: Proceed past a HEALTH_WARN with non-benign checks like PG_DEGRADED, SLOW_OPS, or MON_DOWN. A blocking HEALTH_ERR is fatal regardless of this flag. Checks that ceph reports as muted, and checks known to be harmless for a rolling restart, never block and are named in the task log. ... Default: 0.

only-outdated.description: Restart only OSDs whose running version differs from the locally-installed ceph-osd binary. Useful for post-upgrade rolling restarts that should touch only daemons that need it. Refuses if the local binary version cannot be determined. Ignored on resume (the saved plan is used as-is). Default: 0.

resume.description: Resume an aborted bulk-restart from the checkpoint stored in Ceph's config-key store. The plan and noout decision from the prior run are honored; 'set-noout' is ignored. When false (default), the endpoint refuses to start if a checkpoint exists for this node, to avoid silently overwriting in-progress work. Default: 0.

service-type.description: Ceph daemon type to restart. Only OSDs can be rolling-restarted on a per-node basis.

set-noout.description: Set the 'noout' flag on each OSD targeted by this run for the duration of the rolling restart, and unset it on completion. Per-OSD rather than cluster-wide so that unrelated OSDs failing on other nodes still trigger backfill normally. Default: 1.

timeout.description: Per-OSD timeout (in seconds). Bounds both the wait for a restarted OSD to come back up and the wait for recovery to quiesce enough that Ceph reports the next OSD safe to stop. Default sized for busy clusters where multi-TB OSDs with many PGs can need several minutes to clear peering after a restart; bump higher for very large or heavily-loaded OSDs. Default: 600. Format: <integer> (30 - 1800).

endcursor.description: End before the given Cursor. Conflicts with 'until'

identifiers.description: Also return a record listing the distinct syslog identifiers present, for filter completion. Only honored together with 'structured'. Default: 0.

lastentries.description: Limit to the last X lines. Conflicts with a range. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

priority.description: Only print messages of this syslog priority: a single level from 0 (emerg) to 7 (debug), selecting that level and everything more severe, or a 'LOW..HIGH' range. Empty means no priority filter. Pattern: ^([0-7](\.\.[0-7])?)?$

service.description: Only print messages whose syslog identifier matches this glob, for example 'pve*' or 'postfix/*'. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_.@:*?!\[\]\/-]+$

since.description: Display all log since this UNIX epoch. Conflicts with 'startcursor'. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

startcursor.description: Start after the given Cursor. Conflicts with 'since'

structured.description: Return one JSON object per entry with separate fields (timestamp, identifier, message, priority, ...) instead of pre-rendered text lines. Default: 0.

unit.description: Only print messages of this systemd unit (the .service suffix is implied). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_.@:-]+$

units.description: Also return a record listing the distinct systemd units present, for filter completion. Only honored together with 'structured'. Default: 0.

until.description: Display all log until this UNIX epoch. Conflicts with 'endcursor'. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

name: pve_create_lxc
title: Create lxc
description: Create or restore a container. [POST /nodes/{node}/lxc. Needs: You need 'VM.Allocate' permission on /vms/{vmid} or on the VM pool /pool/{pool}. For restore, it is enough if the user has 'VM.Backup' permission and the VM already exists. You also need 'Datastore.AllocateSpace' .... Destructive with some argument values. These reach the host itself and need PROXMOX_ALLOW_ELEVATED: hookscript, dev[n], mp[n], rootfs, unprivileged. Pass unprivileged=1: left out, Proxmox creates a privileged container, which counts as host access.]

node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

bwlimit.description: Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s). Default: restore limit from datacenter or storage config. Format: <number> (0 - N).

cmode.description: Console mode. By default, the console command tries to open a connection to one of the available tty devices. By setting cmode to 'console' it tries to attach to /dev/console instead. If you set cmode to 'shell', it simply invokes a shell inside the container (no login). Default: tty.

console.description: Attach a console device (/dev/console) to the container. Default: 1.

cores.description: The number of cores assigned to the container. A container can use all available cores by default. Format: <integer> (1 - 8192).

cpulimit.description: Limit of CPU usage. NOTE: If the computer has 2 CPUs, it has a total of '2' CPU time. Value '0' indicates no CPU limit. Default: 0. Format: <number> (0 - 8192).

cpuunits.description: CPU weight for a container, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2. Default: cgroup v1: 1024, cgroup v2: 100. Format: <integer> (0 - 500000).

debug.description: Try to be more verbose. For now this only enables debug log-level on start. Default: 0.

description.description: Description for the Container. Shown in the web-interface CT's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

dev.description: Device to pass through to the container Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): path=<pve-lxc-dev-string> deny-write=<boolean> gid=<integer> mode=<Octal access mode> uid=<integer> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is dev0 in Proxmox, and dev0 is also accepted as an argument.

entrypoint.description: Command to run as init, optionally with arguments; may start with an absolute path, relative path, or a binary in $PATH. Default: /sbin/init. Pattern: (?^:[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]+)

env.description: The container runtime environment as NUL-separated list. Replaces any lxc.environment.runtime entries in the config. Pattern: (?^:(?:\w+=[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]*)(?:\0\w+=[^\x00-\x08\x0a-\x1F\x7F]*)*)

features.description: Allow containers access to advanced features. Property string (key=value,...; * required): force_rw_sys=<boolean> fuse=<boolean> keyctl=<boolean> mknod=<boolean> mount=<fstype;fstype;...> nesting=<boolean>

force.description: Allow to overwrite existing container.

ha-managed.description: Add the CT as a HA resource after it was created. Default: 0.

hookscript.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the containers lifetime.

hostname.description: Set a host name for the container.

ignore-unpack-errors.description: Ignore errors when extracting the template.

memory.description: Amount of RAM for the container in MB. Default: 512. Format: <integer> (16 - N).

mp.description: Use volume as container mount point. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): volume*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> acl=<boolean> backup=<boolean> idmap=<type:container:disk:range-size[;type:container:disk:range-size;...]> keepattrs=<boolean> mountoptions=<opt[;opt...]> mp*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> quota=<boolean> replicate=<boolean> ro=<boolean> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is mp0 in Proxmox, and mp0 is also accepted as an argument.

nameserver.description: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if you neither set searchdomain nor nameserver.

net.description: Specifies network interfaces for the container. Property string (key=value,...; * required): bridge=<bridge> firewall=<boolean> gw=<ipv4> gw6=<ipv6> host-managed=<boolean> hwaddr=<mac-addr> ip=<pve-ipv4-config> ip6=<pve-ipv6-config> link_down=<boolean> mtu=<integer> name*=<string> rate=<mbps> tag=<integer> trunks=<vlanid[;vlanid...]> type=<veth> Numbered items, such as {"0": "virtio,bridge=vmbr0"}: key 0 is net0 in Proxmox, and net0 is also accepted as an argument.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a container will be started during system bootup. Default: 0.

ostemplate.description: The OS template or backup file.

ostype.description: OS type. This is used to setup configuration inside the container, and corresponds to lxc setup scripts in /usr/share/lxc/config/<ostype>.common.conf. Value 'unmanaged' can be used to skip and OS specific setup.

pool.description: Add the VM to the specified pool.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the container. This will prevent the CT or CT's disk remove/update operation. Default: 0.

rootfs.description: Use volume as container root. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): volume*=<pve-lxc-mp-string> acl=<boolean> idmap=<type:container:disk:range-size[;type:container:disk:range-size;...]> mountoptions=<opt[;opt...]> quota=<boolean> replicate=<boolean> ro=<boolean> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size>

searchdomain.description: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if you neither set searchdomain nor nameserver.

ssh-public-keys.description: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

start.description: Start the CT after its creation finished successfully. Default: 0.

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped. Format: [[order=]\d+] [,up=\d+] [,down=\d+] .

storage.description: Default Storage. Default: local. Format: <storage ID>.

swap.description: Amount of SWAP for the container in MB. Default: 512. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

tags.description: Tags of the Container. This is only meta information.

timezone.description: Time zone to use in the container. If option isn't set, then nothing will be done. Can be set to 'host' to match the host time zone, or an arbitrary time zone option from /usr/share/zoneinfo/zone.tab

tty.description: Specify the number of tty available to the container Default: 2. Format: <integer> (0 - 6).

unique.description: Assign a unique random ethernet address. Needs restore.

unprivileged.description: Makes the container run as unprivileged user. For creation, the default is 1. For restore, the default is the value from the backup. (Should not be modified manually.) Default: 0.

unused.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): volume*=<pve-volume-id> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is unused0 in Proxmox, and unused0 is also accepted as an argument.

vmid.description: The (unique) ID of the VM. Format: <integer> (100 - 999999999).

wait.description: If the call starts a task, wait for its end (default true). A failed task is reported as an error.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this it keeps running: see pve_wait_task.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

tty.description: Specify the number of tty available to the container Default: 2. Format: <integer> (0 - 6).

unprivileged.description: Makes the container run as unprivileged user. For creation, the default is 1. For restore, the default is the value from the backup. (Should not be modified manually.) Default: 0.

unused.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. node.description: The cluster node name. Optional when there is a default node or only one node.

affinity.description: List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11

arch.description: Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture.

archive.description: The backup archive. Either the file system path to a .tar or .vma file (use '-' to pipe data from stdin) or a proxmox storage backup volume identifier.

audio0.description: Configure a audio device, useful in combination with QXL/Spice. Property string (key=value,...; * required): device*=<ich9-intel-hda|intel-hda|AC97> driver=<spice|none>

autostart.description: Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored). Default: 0.

balloon.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

boot.description: Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated. Format: [[legacy=]<[acdn]{1,4}>] [,order=<device[;device...]>].

bootdisk.description: Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead. Pattern: (ide|sata|scsi|virtio)\d+

bwlimit.description: Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s). Default: restore limit from datacenter or storage config. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

cdrom.description: This is an alias for option -ide2 Format: <volume>.

cicustom.description: cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start. Format: [meta=<volume>] [,network=<volume>] [,user=<volume>] [,vendor=<volume>].

cipassword.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

citype.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

ciupgrade.description: cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot. Default: 1.

ciuser.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

cores.description: The number of cores per socket. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

cpulimit.description: Limit of CPU usage. Default: 0. Format: <number> (0 - 128).

cpuunits.description: CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2. Default: cgroup v1: 1024, cgroup v2: 100. Format: <integer> (1 - 262144).

description.description: Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

efidisk0.description: Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id-or-qm-path> efitype=<2m|4m> format=<raw|qcow|qed|qcow2|vmdk|cloop> import-from=<pve-volume-id-or-absolute-path> ms-cert=<2011|2023|2023w|2023k> pre-enrolled-keys=<boolean> size=<disk-size>

force.description: Allow to overwrite existing VM. Needs archive.

freeze.description: Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution).

ha-managed.description: Add the VM as a HA resource after it was created. Default: 0.

hookscript.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime.

hostpci.description: Map host PCI devices into guest. Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is hostpci0 in Proxmox, and hostpci0 is also accepted as an argument.

hotplug.description: Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7. Default: network,disk,usb.

hugepages.description: Enables hugepages memory. Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB.

ide.description: Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id-or-qm-path> aio=<native|threads|io_uring> backup=<boolean> bps=<bps> bps_max_length=<seconds> bps_rd=<bps> bps_rd_max_length=<seconds> bps_wr=<bps> bps_wr_max_length=<seconds> cache=<none|writethrough|writeback|unsafe|directsync> detect_zeroes=<boolean> discard=<ignore|on> format=<raw|qcow|qed|qcow2|vmdk|cloop> import-from=<pve-volume-id-or-absolute-path> iops=<iops> iops_max=<iops> iops_max_length=<seconds> iops_rd=<iops> iops_rd_max=<iops> iops_rd_max_length=<seconds> iops_wr=<iops> iops_wr_max=<iops> iops_wr_max_length=<seconds> mbps=<mbps> mbps_max=<mbps> mbps_rd=<mbps> mbps_rd_max=<mbps> mbps_wr=<mbps> mbps_wr_max=<mbps> media=<cdrom|disk> model=<urlencoded> replicate=<boolean> rerror=<ignore|report|stop> serial=<urlencoded> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size> snapshot=<boolean> ssd=<boolean> werror=<enospc|ignore|report|stop> wwn=<wwn> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is ide0 in Proxmox, and ide0 is also accepted as an argument.

import-working-storage.description: A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage. Format: <storage ID>.

intel-tdx.description: Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs Format: [type=]<tdx-type> ,attestation=<1|0> [,vsock-cid=<integer>] [,vsock-port=<integer>].

ipconfig.description: cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface. IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified. ivshmem.description: Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host. Property string (key=value,...; * required): name=<string> size*=<integer>

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts. Default: 0.

keyboard.description: Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. Default: null.

live-restore.description: Start the VM immediately while importing or restoring in the background.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

machine.description: Specify the QEMU machine. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<machine type> aw-bits=<number> enable-s3=<boolean> enable-s4=<boolean> viommu=<intel|virtio>

memory.description: Memory properties. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): current*=<integer>

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU). Default: 0.1. Format: <number> (0 - N).

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

net.description: Specify network devices. numa_n.description: NUMA topology. Property string (key=value,...; * required): cpus*=<id[-id];...> hostnodes=<id[-id];...> memory=<number> policy=<preferred|bind|interleave> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is numa0 in Proxmox, and numa0 is also accepted as an argument.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup. Default: 0.

ostype.description: Specify guest operating system. Default: other.

parallel.description: Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2). Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is parallel0 in Proxmox, and parallel0 is also accepted as an argument.

pool.description: Add the VM to the specified pool.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations. Default: 0.

reboot.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot. Default: 1.

searchdomain.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

serial.description: Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3) Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is serial0 in Proxmox, and serial0 is also accepted as an argument.

shares.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd. Default: 1000. Format: <integer> (0 - 50000).

smp.description: The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

sockets.description: The number of CPU sockets. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

spice_enhancements.description: Configure additional enhancements for SPICE. Property string (key=value,...; * required): foldersharing=<boolean> videostreaming=<off|all|filter>

sshkeys.description: cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

start.description: Start VM after it was created successfully. Default: 0.

startdate.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'. Default: now. Format: (now | YYYY-MM-DD | YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Pattern: (now|\d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}(T\d{1,2}:\d{1,2}:\d{1,2})?)

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped. Format: [[order=]\d+] [,up=\d+] [,down=\d+] .

tablet.description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device. Default: 1.

tags.description: Tags of the VM. This is only meta information.

tpmstate0.description: Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. unique.description: Assign a unique random ethernet address. Needs archive.

unused.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is unused0 in Proxmox, and unused0 is also accepted as an argument.

usb.description: Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7, n can be up to 14). vcpus.description: Number of hotplugged vcpus. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

vga.description: Configure the VGA hardware. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<cirrus|qxl|qxl2|qxl3|qxl4|none|serial0|serial1|serial2|serial3|std|virtio|virtio-gl|vmware> clipboard=<vnc> memory=<integer>

virtio.description: Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. virtiofs.description: Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs. vmgenid.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly. Default: 1 (autogenerated). Pattern: (?:[a-fA-F0-9]{8}(?:-[a-fA-F0-9]{4}){3}-[a-fA-F0-9]{12}|[01])

vmstatestorage.description: Default storage for VM state volumes/files. Format: <storage ID>.

watchdog.description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device. Format: [[model=]<i6300esb|ib700>] [,action=<enum>].

balloon.description: Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

boot.description: Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated. Format: [[legacy=]<[acdn]{1,4}>] [,order=<device[;device...]>].

bootdisk.description: Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead. Pattern: (ide|sata|scsi|virtio)\d+

cdrom.description: This is an alias for option -ide2 Format: <volume>.

cicustom.description: cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start. Format: [meta=<volume>] [,network=<volume>] [,user=<volume>] [,vendor=<volume>].

cipassword.description: cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords.

citype.description: Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows.

ciupgrade.description: cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot. Default: 1.

ciuser.description: cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user.

cores.description: The number of cores per socket. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

cpulimit.description: Limit of CPU usage. Default: 0. Format: <number> (0 - 128).

cpuunits.description: CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2. Default: cgroup v1: 1024, cgroup v2: 100. Format: <integer> (1 - 262144).

delete.description: A list of settings you want to delete.

description.description: Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file.

digest.description: Prevent changes if current configuration file has different SHA1 digest. This can be used to prevent concurrent modifications.

efidisk0.description: Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id-or-qm-path> efitype=<2m|4m> format=<raw|qcow|qed|qcow2|vmdk|cloop> import-from=<pve-volume-id-or-absolute-path> ms-cert=<2011|2023|2023w|2023k> pre-enrolled-keys=<boolean> size=<disk-size>

force.description: Force physical removal. Without this, we simple remove the disk from the config file and create an additional configuration entry called 'unused[n]', which contains the volume ID. Unlink of unused[n] always cause physical removal. Needs delete.

freeze.description: Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution).

hookscript.description: Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime.

hostpci.description: Map host PCI devices into guest. Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is hostpci0 in Proxmox, and hostpci0 is also accepted as an argument.

hotplug.description: Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7. Default: network,disk,usb.

hugepages.description: Enables hugepages memory. Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB.

ide.description: Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. import-working-storage.description: A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage. Format: <storage ID>.

intel-tdx.description: Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs Format: [type=]<tdx-type> ,attestation=<1|0> [,vsock-cid=<integer>] [,vsock-port=<integer>].

ipconfig.description: cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface. IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified. The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided. For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. ... Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is ipconfig0 in Proxmox, and ipconfig0 is also accepted as an argument.

ivshmem.description: Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host. Property string (key=value,...; * required): name=<string> size*=<integer>

keephugepages.description: Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts. Default: 0.

keyboard.description: Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. Default: null.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

machine.description: Specify the QEMU machine. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<machine type> aw-bits=<number> enable-s3=<boolean> enable-s4=<boolean> viommu=<intel|virtio>

memory.description: Memory properties. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): current*=<integer>

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU). Default: 0.1. Format: <number> (0 - N).

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

net.description: Specify network devices. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): model*=<e1000|e1000-82540em|e1000-82544gc|e1000-82545em|e1000e|i82551|i82557b|i82559er|ne2k_isa|ne2k_pci|pcnet|rtl8139|virtio|vmxnet3> bridge=<pve-bridge-id> firewall=<boolean> host-tunnel=<boolean> link_down=<boolean> macaddr=<mac-addr> mtu=<integer> queues=<integer> rate=<number> tag=<integer> trunks=<vlanid[;vlanid...]> Numbered items, such as {"0": "virtio,bridge=vmbr0"}: key 0 is net0 in Proxmox, and net0 is also accepted as an argument.

numa_n.description: NUMA topology. Property string (key=value,...; * required): cpus*=<id[-id];...> hostnodes=<id[-id];...> memory=<number> policy=<preferred|bind|interleave> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is numa0 in Proxmox, and numa0 is also accepted as an argument.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup. Default: 0.

ostype.description: Specify guest operating system. Default: other.

parallel.description: Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2). Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is parallel0 in Proxmox, and parallel0 is also accepted as an argument.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations. Default: 0.

reboot.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot. Default: 1.

rng0.description: Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator. Format: [source=]</dev/urandom|/dev/random|/dev/hwrng> [,max_bytes=<integer>] [,period=<integer>].

sata.description: Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. scsi.description: Use volume as SCSI hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 30). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. searchdomain.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

serial.description: Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3) Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is serial0 in Proxmox, and serial0 is also accepted as an argument.

shares.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd. Default: 1000. Format: <integer> (0 - 50000).

skiplock.description: Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option.

smp.description: The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

sockets.description: The number of CPU sockets. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

spice_enhancements.description: Configure additional enhancements for SPICE. Property string (key=value,...; * required): foldersharing=<boolean> videostreaming=<off|all|filter>

sshkeys.description: cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

startdate.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'. Default: now. Format: (now | YYYY-MM-DD | YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Pattern: (now|\d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}(T\d{1,2}:\d{1,2}:\d{1,2})?)

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped. Format: [[order=]\d+] [,up=\d+] [,down=\d+] .

tablet.description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device. Default: 1.

tags.description: Tags of the VM. This is only meta information.

tpmstate0.description: Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id-or-qm-path> format=<raw|qcow2|vmdk> import-from=<pve-volume-id-or-absolute-path> size=<disk-size> version=<v1.2|v2.0>

unused.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is unused0 in Proxmox, and unused0 is also accepted as an argument.

usb.description: Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7, n can be up to 14). Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): host=<HOSTUSBDEVICE|spice> mapping=<pve-configid> usb3=<boolean> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is usb0 in Proxmox, and usb0 is also accepted as an argument.

vcpus.description: Number of hotplugged vcpus. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

vga.description: Configure the VGA hardware. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<cirrus|qxl|qxl2|qxl3|qxl4|none|serial0|serial1|serial2|serial3|std|virtio|virtio-gl|vmware> clipboard=<vnc> memory=<integer>

virtio.description: Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): file*=<pve-volume-id-or-qm-path> aio=<native|threads|io_uring> backup=<boolean> bps=<bps> bps_max_length=<seconds> bps_rd=<bps> bps_rd_max_length=<seconds> bps_wr=<bps> bps_wr_max_length=<seconds> cache=<none|writethrough|writeback|unsafe|directsync> detect_zeroes=<boolean> discard=<ignore|on> format=<raw|qcow|qed|qcow2|vmdk|cloop> import-from=<pve-volume-id-or-absolute-path> iops=<iops> iops_max=<iops> iops_max_length=<seconds> iops_rd=<iops> iops_rd_max=<iops> iops_rd_max_length=<seconds> iops_wr=<iops> iops_wr_max=<iops> iops_wr_max_length=<seconds> iothread=<boolean> mbps=<mbps> mbps_max=<mbps> mbps_rd=<mbps> mbps_rd_max=<mbps> mbps_wr=<mbps> mbps_wr_max=<mbps> media=<cdrom|disk> replicate=<boolean> rerror=<ignore|report|stop> ro=<boolean> serial=<urlencoded> shared=<boolean> size=<disk-size> snapshot=<boolean> werror=<enospc|ignore|report|stop> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is virtio0 in Proxmox, and virtio0 is also accepted as an argument.

virtiofs.description: Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): dirid*=<pve-configid> cache=<auto|always|metadata|never> direct-io=<boolean> expose-acl=<boolean> expose-xattr=<boolean> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is virtiofs0 in Proxmox, and virtiofs0 is also accepted as an argument.

vmgenid.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly. Default: 1 (autogenerated). Pattern: (?:[a-fA-F0-9]{8}(?:-[a-fA-F0-9]{4}){3}-[a-fA-F0-9]{12}|[01])

vmstatestorage.description: Default storage for VM state volumes/files. Format: <storage ID>.

watchdog.description: Create a virtual hardware watchdog device. Format: [[model=]<i6300esb|ib700>] [,action=<enum>].

wait.description: If the call starts a task, wait for its end (default true). A failed task is reported as an error.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30). Past this it keeps running: see pve_wait_task.

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.

description: Set virtual machine options (synchronous API) - You should consider using the POST method instead for any actions involving hotplug or storage allocation. [PUT /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/config. Needs: VM.Config.Disk, VM.Config.CDROM, VM.Config.CPU, VM.Config.Memory, VM.Config.Network, VM.Config.HWType, VM.Config.Options, VM.Config.Cloudinit (any of) on /vms/{vmid}. Destructive with some argument values. These reach the host itself and need PROXMOX_ALLOW_ELEVATED: hookscript, args, hostpci[n], parallel[n], usb[n], serial[n].]

affinity.description: List of host cores used to execute guest processes, for example: 0,5,8-11

agent.description: Enable/disable communication with the QEMU Guest Agent and its properties. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): enabled*=<boolean> freeze-fs=<boolean> fstrim_cloned_disks=<boolean> type=<virtio|isa>

allow-ksm.description: Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging). Default: 1.

keyboard.description: Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. Default: null.

localtime.description: Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS.

machine.description: Specify the QEMU machine. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<machine type> aw-bits=<number> enable-s3=<boolean> enable-s4=<boolean> viommu=<intel|virtio>

memory.description: Memory properties. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): current*=<integer>

migrate_downtime.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU). Default: 0.1. Format: <number> (0 - N).

migrate_speed.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

name.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

nameserver.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

net.description: Specify network devices. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): model*=<e1000|e1000-82540em|e1000-82544gc|e1000-82545em|e1000e|i82551|i82557b|i82559er|ne2k_isa|ne2k_pci|pcnet|rtl8139|virtio|vmxnet3> bridge=<pve-bridge-id> firewall=<boolean> host-tunnel=<boolean> link_down=<boolean> macaddr=<mac-addr> mtu=<integer> queues=<integer> rate=<number> tag=<integer> trunks=<vlanid[;vlanid...]> Numbered items, such as {"0": "virtio,bridge=vmbr0"}: key 0 is net0 in Proxmox, and net0 is also accepted as an argument.

numa_n.description: NUMA topology. Property string (key=value,...; * required): cpus*=<id[-id];...> hostnodes=<id[-id];...> memory=<number> policy=<preferred|bind|interleave> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is numa0 in Proxmox, and numa0 is also accepted as an argument.

onboot.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup. Default: 0.

ostype.description: Specify guest operating system. Default: other.

parallel.description: Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2). Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is parallel0 in Proxmox, and parallel0 is also accepted as an argument.

protection.description: Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations. Default: 0.

reboot.description: Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot. Default: 1.

rng0.description: Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator. Format: [source=]</dev/urandom|/dev/random|/dev/hwrng> [,max_bytes=<integer>] [,period=<integer>].

sata.description: Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. searchdomain.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

serial.description: Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3) Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is serial0 in Proxmox, and serial0 is also accepted as an argument.

shares.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd. Default: 1000. Format: <integer> (0 - 50000).

skiplock.description: Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option.

smp.description: The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

sockets.description: The number of CPU sockets. Default: 1. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

spice_enhancements.description: Configure additional enhancements for SPICE. Property string (key=value,...; * required): foldersharing=<boolean> videostreaming=<off|all|filter>

sshkeys.description: cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format).

startdate.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'. Default: now. Format: (now | YYYY-MM-DD | YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Pattern: (now|\d{4}-\d{1,2}-\d{1,2}(T\d{1,2}:\d{1,2}:\d{1,2})?)

startup.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped. Format: [[order=]\d+] [,up=\d+] [,down=\d+] .

tablet.description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device. Default: 1.

tags.description: Tags of the VM. This is only meta information.

tpmstate0.description: Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. unused.description: Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. usb.description: Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version >= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows > 7, n can be up to 14). vcpus.description: Number of hotplugged vcpus. Default: 0. Format: <integer> (1 - N).

vga.description: Configure the VGA hardware. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): type=<cirrus|qxl|qxl2|qxl3|qxl4|none|serial0|serial1|serial2|serial3|std|virtio|virtio-gl|vmware> clipboard=<vnc> memory=<integer>

virtio.description: Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. virtiofs.description: Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs. Property string (key=value,...; * required; the name of the first key can be left out): dirid*=<pve-configid> cache=<auto|always|metadata|never> direct-io=<boolean> expose-acl=<boolean> expose-xattr=<boolean> Numbered items, such as {"0": "..."}: key 0 is virtiofs0 in Proxmox, and virtiofs0 is also accepted as an argument.

vmgenid.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly. Default: 1 (autogenerated). Pattern: (?:[a-fA-F0-9]{8}(?:-[a-fA-F0-9]{4}){3}-[a-fA-F0-9]{12}|[01])

dest.description: Restrict packet destination address. This can refer to a single IP address, an IP set ('+ipsetname') or an IP alias definition. Please do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 addresses inside such lists.

iface.description: Network interface name. You have to use network configuration key names for VMs and containers ('net\d+'). Host related rules can use arbitrary strings.

pos.description: Update rule at position <pos>. Format: <integer> (0 - N).

proto.description: IP protocol. You can use protocol names ('tcp'/'udp') or simple numbers, as defined in '/etc/protocols'.

source.description: Restrict packet source address. This can refer to a single IP address, an IP set ('+ipsetname') or an IP alias definition. You can also specify an address range like '20.34.101.207-201.3.9.99', or a list of IP addresses and networks (entries are separated by comma). Please do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 addresses inside such lists.

sport.description: Restrict TCP/UDP source port. You can use service names or simple numbers (0-65535), as defined in '/etc/services'. Port ranges can be specified with '\d+:\d+', for example '80:85', and you can use comma separated list to match several ports or ranges.

bwlimit.description: Set I/O bandwidth limit for various operations (in KiB/s). Property string (key=value,...; * required): clone=<LIMIT> default=<LIMIT> migration=<LIMIT> move=<LIMIT> restore=<LIMIT>

encryption-key.description: Encryption key. Use 'autogen' to generate one automatically without passphrase.

krbd.description: Always access rbd through krbd kernel module. Default: 0.

lio_tpg.description: target portal group for Linux LIO targets

master-pubkey.description: Base64-encoded, PEM-formatted public RSA key. Used to encrypt a copy of the encryption-key which will be added to each encrypted backup.

max-protected-backups.description: Maximal number of protected backups per guest. Use '-1' for unlimited. Default: Unlimited for users with Datastore.Allocate privilege, 5 for other users. Format: <integer> (-1 - N).

mkdir.description: Create the directory if it doesn't exist and populate it with default sub-dirs. NOTE: Deprecated, use the 'create-base-path' and 'create-subdirs' options instead. Default: yes.

monhost.description: IP addresses of monitors (for external clusters).

nowritecache.description: disable write caching on the target

We say that backups within this period are covered by this option. The next option does not take care of already covered backups and only considers older backups.

title: Describe an API method
description: Gives everything known about one API method: all parameters with types and allowed values, privileges needed, what it returns, the gate this server applies and the tool that calls it. Use this before a call that failed validation, or to build a property string such as net0.

path.description: The template (/nodes/{node}/qemu), or a concrete path (/nodes/pve1/qemu).

name: pve_api_read
title: Read any API path
description: Calls any GET method by path, under the same policy as the dedicated tools: gate read, or sensitive when that is allowed. For what is not in your tool list. A path that is not in the catalog counts as sensitive. Secrets are redacted.

path.description: API path, without /api2/json, such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config. It may also be a template with {placeholders}, filled from path_params.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path. The way to pass a value holding a slash, such as a volume id: path /nodes/pve1/storage/local/content/{volume}, path_params {"volume": "local:iso/x.iso"}.

params.description: Parameters. Booleans become 1/0, arrays repeat the key, and {"0": "..."} under net becomes net0.

page_limit.description: Rows per page, when the answer is a list.

page_offset.description: Rows to skip. Use next_offset from the previous page.

name: pve_api_write
title: Write to any API path
description: Calls any POST, PUT or DELETE method by path, for what is not in your tool list. The same policy applies: the gate of the method is checked, including elevated, guest_exec and console, and blocked endpoints stay blocked. A path that is not in the catalog counts as elevated. A task id in the answer is waited for. Prefer a dedicated tool whenever one exists.

path.description: API path, without /api2/json, such as /nodes/pve1/qemu/100/config. It may also be a template with {placeholders}, filled from path_params.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path. The way to pass a value holding a slash, such as a volume id: path /nodes/pve1/storage/local/content/{volume}, path_params {"volume": "local:iso/x.iso"}.

params.description: Parameters. Booleans become 1/0, arrays repeat the key, and {"0": "..."} under net becomes net0.

wait.description: If the call starts a task, wait for its end (default true).

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task. Default: PROXMOX_TASK_WAIT_SECONDS (30).

dry_run.description: Show what would be sent without sending anything.
